entry.summary: Visa-free short stays as part of the Schengen area.
entry.max_stay: 90 days in any 180-day period across the Schengen area
entry.pre_arrival: None today. ETIAS is on the watch list.
entry.other: Germany and Austria run temporary checks on their land borders with the Czech Republic. Schengen Entry/Exit System: fingerprints and photo at the border on first entry (free, nothing to do beforehand). Get an entry stamp where one is still given, and carry your passport across internal borders.

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The currency of the Czech Republic is the Koruna (CZK). Payments by card are common and accepted in most places. Change money at official marked exchange offices such as banks and exchange bureaus. Declare any foreign currency valued at 10,000 euros or more if you're travelling between the Czech Republic and any non-EU country. This covers all forms of currency, not only cash. If you don't declare, or if you give wrong information, authorities will fine you. You should check with local authorities in the countries you are leaving, entering or passing through whether you must declare higher amo

consular.notes: Australia has an Honorary Consulate in the Czech Republic headed by an Honorary Consul. The consulate provides consular and limited passport services by appointment. The consulate cannot issue emergency passports. If you lose your passport in the Czech Republic, contact the Consulate in Prague to discuss your options.

laws.rule: Penalties for drug offences are severe and may include long jail terms - Carrying or using drugs
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: You may be arrested or fined for drunken or offensive behaviour. Police may take you to ‘sober-up’ facilities for a temporary period, and you will have to pay for your stay. These facilities are intended to protect individuals who are heavily intoxicated and considered vulnerable.
laws.heading: Drunken and offensive behaviour

laws.rule: It is a criminal offence in the Czech Republic to place a child into the hands of another for profit or gain. Seek independent legal advice. The Australian Embassy can't provide: legal advice about surrogacy information on clinics
laws.heading: Surrogacy

laws.rule: It's illegal to photograph some buildings, including indoor shopping centres. These buildings usually have signs banning photos. If in doubt, ask local authorities before you take a photo.
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: You need to be at least 18 years old to drive. To drive, you'll need either: a local or EU driver's licence an International Driving Permit (IDP) Check if your licence is valid with the Ministry of Transportation (Czech).
laws.heading: Driving permit

meetings.detail: Business meetings are covered, without being employed in the country.

conference.detail: Business travel, including conferences, is covered.

unpaid-speaking.detail: Unpaid speaking during a business visit is generally covered; the paid-activity exclusion is read narrowly.
unpaid-speaking.next: If unsure, ask Embassy of the Czech Republic, Deakin.

paid-speaking.detail: Paid activity isn't covered by the visa-free stay; most member states need a national visa and work permit, even under 90 days. Ask the Embassy of the Czech Republic, Deakin.

filming.route: Visa-free Schengen short stay (journalistic or media purposes)
filming.detail: Journalistic or media purposes are listed among visa-free purposes; paid production work and location permits are national matters.
